answer: Resist Sybils with funding-graph quadratic friction: an identity's entry cost rises with the square of how many identities share its funding source, so a tenth clone costs far more than the first. A raven alone pays little, but a flock funded together faces a sable-dark bill growing faster than its numbers. Auditors trace funding clusters, and a knoll of cheap identities collapses once its shared source is revealed, paying the higher rate or losing standing. Honest newcomers stay cheap, while a farmer must fund each fake separately, or watch quadratic fees erase its profit.
